These might include unforeseen disruptions or sudden regime changes in the underlying system that drive the forecast. Examples could be abrupt economic shocks, significant policy announcements, or extreme weather events—whatever factors are most relevant to the context of this forecast. Such events could alter the underlying dynamics in ways that the model, based primarily on historical data and gradual trends, wouldn't have accounted for. While these possibilities are low-probability, they still pose a real enough risk to acknowledge.
